Subject: Request: evidence and handover for UK IDTA/TIA

Hi Markus / Kimberly / Laura,

Thanks for the call last week. Procurement at Blue Ocean needs a compact evidence package to close the DPA/TIA checklist for our UK pilot (we'll be signing the UK addendum). Specifically they asked for: 

- A mapping of which token streams and logs are covered by the TIA, with sequence-level examples (we need the TIA mapping as an artifact).
- The current subprocessor list (csv) and confirmation of any planned changes in the next 90 days.
- A short note (1–2 pages) describing residency failover behavior and how onshore caching/proxying is audited — procurement wants to see controls for a documented fallback.

Can you share the artifacts and an estimated timeline? Legal would like to review the technical notes before we route to our internal privacy committee. We prefer a consolidated package (single ZIP) rather than multiple emails.

Also copying procurement (procurement@blueoceanhealth.com) and David Chen from vendor ops.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — target is to have DocuSign-ready materials by the end of next week (10 Mar).

Best,
Elaine Torres
Legal Operations
Blue Ocean Health

Hi all — quick technical note to accompany the artifacts Markus plans to send. Putting this here so legal/procurement have context before Laura reviews wording.

Summary (short):
- Proxying / onshore cache fallback: our runtime supports region-specific prefix caching and a configured onshore cache node for UK-region traffic. Failover behavior is deterministic: if primary EU routing fails, requests are routed to the onshore cache node which returns cached responses when available; otherwise they fall back to a compatible quantized model variant in the nearest compliant region.
- Auditing & controls: every failover event is captured in an immutable audit log (tokenized identifiers, not raw payload). Logs are retained per customer for the agreed retention period in the DPA and are available as part of the TIA evidence package. We also include a sample SIEM export template.
- Key custody & KMS: customer-managed keys are supported via our KMS integration; HSM-backed keystore attestations are in the evidence bucket when enabled.

What I will attach: a 2-page controls memo (residency-failover-controls.pdf) and a sample SIEM export excerpt.

Request for Blue Ocean: please share the exact fields you want in the subprocessor CSV (procurement templates often have extra columns like region_of_processing, purpose, contact). If you need the bridge-letter language that explicitly names the onshore cache node and SLA for failover, Laura can draft that once we confirm the technical descriptors.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure & Compliance
Redwood Inference
